thesis: Pacific Cleaning Services may bear premises-maintenance liability for the wet floor, but the party is not yet confirmed and its insurer is unknown.

supporting_evidence.quote: Park states the floor was wet and she did not see a wet floor sign.
supporting_evidence.claim: Claimant alleges a wet floor with no warning signage at the time of loss.

supporting_evidence.quote: Brewline contracts cleaning to Pacific Cleaning Services (Lynnwood WA).
supporting_evidence.claim: Identifies a third-party contractor potentially responsible for floor maintenance.

supporting_evidence.source: Initial Witness Statement: Brewline Barista Maya Olsen
supporting_evidence.claim: Employee witness did not observe a wet-floor sign in place after the cleaning.

contradicting_evidence.source: Initial Witness Statement: Brewline Barista Maya Olsen
contradicting_evidence.quote: The floor was a little wet near where she fell.
contradicting_evidence.claim: Witness describes only a small amount of water and did not directly confirm the signage was absent.

contradicting_evidence.quote: No video footage; the security camera near the counter was non-operational at the time.
contradicting_evidence.claim: No objective record of the floor condition or signage exists.

estimated_recovery_basis: Initial Swedish ED bill of $14,200; future treatment may increase exposure.
open_questions: Obtain Pacific Cleaning Services' certificate of insurance and liability carrier.
Confirm whether Pacific had wet-floor signage out at the time of the fall.
Determine whether Brewline's contract with Pacific contains a hold-harmless clause.
Verify the time gap between the mopping and the fall.
reviewer_warnings: WA is a pure comparative-negligence state; the claimant's own care may reduce recovery.
The third party's liability insurer is unknown — confirm coverage before issuing a demand.
